rules: Import `ruststream_nats::prelude::*` at a mount site; a handler body imports `ruststream::prelude::*` and bounds its slot on a capability, except a body that writes a per-message JetStream setting (Components: Prelude).

Pick the descriptor by what a subscription reads: bare `#[subscriber("orders.created")]` or `CoreSubject` for one subject, `CoreWildcard` for a `*` or `>` pattern, `JetStreamSubject::new(subject, stream)` for a stream (Components: Subscriptions).
Share Core NATS work with `queue_group(name)` and stream work with `JetStreamSubject::durable(name)`; each message then goes to one member (Components: queue_group, durable).

Settle a JetStream delivery with the handler's outcome and size `ack_wait` above the slowest handler; a Core NATS delivery is processed at most once (Components: Acknowledgement, ack_wait, At most once).
Cap redeliveries with `.max_attempts(n).dead_letter(subject)` after `include`; the framework counts the attempts and publishes the spent delivery (Components: Retries, Dead letters).

Mount a `CoreWildcard` handler with `.out_retry(Publish).to(subject)` or a transform declaring `Names`, the subject its delayed copies go to; without one the app refuses to start (Components: out_retry).

Publish plain Core NATS with `Publish`, the default policy that also makes requests, and store a message in a stream with `JetStreamPublish::default().expect_stream("NAME")` (Components: NatsPublish, JetStreamPublish).
Write `message_id` and the `expect_last_*` steps on the publish builder, with the slot bounded `Out<impl Publisher<Options = JetStreamOptions>, Marker>` (Components: message_id, Expectations).

Send a request with `request(msg, timeout)` on an `Out<impl RequestReply, Slot>` bound to `Publish`, and answer one on the inbox read from `ctx.headers().reply_to()` (Components: RequestReply, Responders).
Read JetStream metadata by binding a `ruststream_nats::context::keys` key as a `Ctx<K>` parameter; every key reads `None` on a Core NATS delivery (Components: JetStreamContext).

Test a service by handing the app `main` runs to `TestApp::start`, which connects `NatsBroker` in process with the `testing` feature, and address it as `tb.broker::<NatsBroker>()` (Components: Testing).
Run the in-process test body against a running server with `TestApp::start_live` for what only a server has: stream configuration, `max_ack_pending`, authentication and TLS (Components: Live).
Attach credentials, TLS and client tuning as `async_nats::ConnectOptions` with `NatsBroker::with_options` (Components: ConnectOptions, Security).
